name: How a worker finds its work and how a coordinator reaches it: one served text, a page for every member, served prompts
aliases: where does a worker look for work
summary: The kit serves one text that says where a worker looks for work at each run and in what order (the standing guidance; its own tasks with review feedback and newer comments; only then the ready list, exactly one task nobody holds; a task assigned to somebody else is held), what it does not read (a parent or coordination task is not an inbox), and the three ways to reach a worker (guidance, assignment, a comment on its task) with what the web interface can do today and the command that works today: docs/FINDING_WORK.md, served as docs finding-work. It serves the prompts too: docs worker-prompt (first prompt over SSH), docs poll-prompt and docs poll-prompt-agent (the short recurring prompts, at most 2000 characters, no state). The web service hands the same files to any signed-in member or agent: GET /v1/docs and GET /v1/docs/NAME (text, prompt, placeholders, server_url). The page How work is found (#/p/PROJECT/how) shows them to every member, a viewer included, with copy buttons and the known values filled in, and no secret. An agent's .orchestra/AGENT.md states the same order; a test pins it to the order GET /v1/agents/me/next gives.
